import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.metrics import r2_score

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Filter the dataset to find the relevant series names
relevant_series_names = [
    'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)',
    'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)',
    'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)',
    'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'
]

# Filter the dataset to include only the relevant series names
df_relevant = df[df['Series Name'].isin(relevant_series_names)]

# Convert all numeric columns to float to ensure they are numeric
for col in df_relevant.columns:
    if col not in ['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name']:
        df_relevant[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_relevant[col], errors='coerce')

# Melt the dataset to have one row per country, year, and variable
df_melted = df_relevant.melt(id_vars=['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name'], 
                             var_name='Year', 
                             value_name='Value')

# Pivot the dataset to have one row per country and year
df_pivot = df_melted.pivot_table(index=['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Year'], 
                                 columns='Series Name', 
                                 values='Value')

# Reset the index to make the pivot table easier to work with
df_pivot = df_pivot.reset_index()

# Rename the columns for clarity
df_pivot.columns = ['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Year'] + [col for col in df_pivot.columns[3:]]

# Drop rows with missing values
df_pivot = df_pivot.dropna()

# Prepare the data for regression
X = df_pivot[['Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)', 
              'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)', 
              'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)']]
y = df_pivot['Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)']

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
r2 = r2_score(y, model.predict(X))

coefficients, r2
